strengths: The paper addresses an important evaluation problem for brain-to-text generation: repeated stimuli and shared subjects can make reported performance misleading about generalization to new subjects and new text. This is directly relevant to NLP evaluation and multimodal language generation.

The experiments cover both Narratives fMRI and ZuCo EEG, with UniCoRN and EEG2Text. The reported differences warrant investigation: under the same nominal UniCoRN training settings, Table 2 shows BLEU-4 of 15.60 for random-frame splitting versus 0.99 for task splitting.

Joint subject and stimulus exclusion is appropriate for the stated generalization objective. The discussion of overlapping fMRI windows identifies an additional source of dependence, and the split taxonomy and diagrams help explain the problem.
weaknesses: The supplied algorithms do not enforce the central zero-contamination guarantee as written. Algorithm 1, line 15, checks the subject endpoint when restoring edges but permits stimuli assigned to validation/test to enter training. Algorithm 2, line 33, checks the task endpoint but permits held-out subjects to enter training. The initialization loops also conflict with the prose and array dimensions. Corrected executable algorithms and explicit checks of pairwise subject/stimulus disjointness are needed to substantiate Table 1.

The experiments do not establish the claimed encoder degradation or signal-independent decoder memorization. Declining validation loss and improving evaluation scores with additional training are not themselves evidence of overfitting. A randomly initialized encoder still receives brain signals and is not a no-signal control. Table 2 also changes initialization, learning rate, and training duration together, while split changes alter generalization difficulty and potentially retained data volume. Matched experiments with shuffled or absent brain signals, controlled training budgets, and a common evaluation target are needed to isolate the proposed mechanisms.

The leakage metrics are not sufficiently well defined to reproduce their interpretation. Equation (7) intersects individual signal frames, although the paper defines cognitive leakage through shared subject identity; distinct recordings from the same subject need not intersect. Its training-count denominator can also be zero for a held-out subject, without a specified convention. The definitions should clearly distinguish subject overlap, exact recording overlap, stimulus identity, and repeated occurrences before their numerical values can support the contamination claims.

There is a concrete inconsistency in the reported generation metrics. Table 3 gives UniCoRN at 80 epochs under method (c) ROUGE-1 F=84.64, P=63.16, and R=71.50. These cannot arise from standard, consistently aggregated F1, precision, and recall; the harmonic mean of the reported P and R is approximately 67.07. This requires correction and an audit of the evaluation implementation.

The framing overgeneralizes beyond the stated objective. Jointly unseen subjects and stimuli define a useful evaluation setting, but within-subject decoding of unseen text is also legitimate. Subject overlap alone does not invalidate an evaluation designed for that setting. Claims that all existing splits are contaminated should distinguish inappropriate overlap for a particular generalization claim from valid evaluation of a different deployment setting.

The claimed benchmark is insufficiently reproducible from the supplied manuscript. Although Appendix A gives some hyperparameters, there is no benchmark access link or exact split manifest, no retained/discarded sample counts, and no clear inference protocol specifying whether reference tokens are supplied. Generation results lack uncertainty across split assignments or training seeds; the four-seed analysis concerns leakage rates only. These omissions matter especially with just 12 ZuCo subjects. Together with the algorithmic and evidential issues above, these are soundness and reproducibility gaps that determine my OA of 2, Resubmit next cycle.
